description: baseline: lora_train.py as-is defaults (lora_r=256 q,v target modules, lr=2e-4, batch=16, context=full, no df), 10 epochs, best at epoch 7
exp01: baseline + --pos-weight (inverse-freq st2/st3 BCE reweighting), 10 epochs, best at epoch 9; adopting pos-weight as new standing default for future experiments

exp02: exp01 + lora_r 256->64 + target-modules query,value->query,key,value,dense (dense matches attn.output.dense AND FFN intermediate/output.dense, so this also LoRA-adapts the FFN -- confounds rank change with module coverage change, but net improvement is large). Note: ~7min/epoch (vs ~2min baseline) due to FFN LoRA adapters on 3072-dim matrices; adopting as new standing default

exp03: exp02 but attention-only (query,key,value,attention.output.dense, excludes FFN intermediate/output.dense) at same lora_r=64. Confirms FFN LoRA adapters are doing real work (0.588 vs exp02's 0.613), not just an rank-change artifact; back at ~2min/epoch though. Reverting to exp02 recipe as standing default

exp04: exp02 recipe with lora_r 64->32, STOPPED after epoch 7/10 (GPU needed elsewhere, not a crash) -- st3=0.523 already beats exp02's st3=0.503 at that point, so this could be competitive or better than exp02 if let run to completion; re-run to full 10 epochs when GPU is free rather than treating as a settled discard
